content.text:
I fixed the bug: emphasis inside a rejected reference link now renders. All tests pass: 1789 spec tests and 45 unit tests.

**Cause.** Before parsing a line, `Lexer.inlineTokens` makes a hidden copy of the text where every reference link whose ref is defined is blanked out as `[aaaa…]`. That copy is what the emphasis code looks at, so it doesn't pair `*` or `_` across link boundaries. Later, when the reference link is rejected because its text contains another link (`outputLink` in `src/Tokenizer.ts`), the `[` is treated as plain text, but that stretch of the copy stays blanked out. The `*`, `_` and `**` inside are hidden, so they never pair and get printed as literal characters.

**Fix (all in `src/Lexer.ts`).**
- I moved the existing masking code, unchanged, into a private method `maskInlineSrc`.
- I added a private method `unmaskRejectedReflink`. It runs when the reference-link tokenizer declines a match, just before the emphasis step. If the text at that point starts with a reference link that is still blanked out in the copy, it rebuilds that stretch by masking only what's inside it. Emphasis inside then works. Links nested inside, such as `[baz][ref]` in example 533, stay masked as before.
- Any other case leaves the copy unchanged, so successful links and undefined refs behave as before.

**Tests.**
- CommonMark example 533 now passes, so I removed its `"shouldFail": true` flag in both `test/specs/commonmark/` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`.
- I added `test/specs/new/reflink_rejected_emphasis.{md,html}`. It covers the `*`, `_` and `**` forms from the report, an inner reference link, and a normal reference link with emphasis that should be unaffected.

I couldn't run eslint because the command was denied.

Separately, `![foo *bar [baz](/url) qux*][ref]` gives the image alt text `foo bar [baz](/url) qux`. My change doesn't cause or touch this, and I left it alone. I believe CommonMark would give `foo bar baz qux`, but I didn't check that against the reference implementation.
